llm.reply:
The gene KRAS encodes a protein belonging to the small GTPase superfamily [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. The protein functions as a molecular switch that persistently activates downstream cellular pathways when mutated [26: "acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways"].

## Enzymatic Activity

The official OMIM record designates the product as KRAS PROTOONCOGENE, GTPase; KRAS [4]. The gene produces a member of the small GTPase superfamily [11: "member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. Single amino acid substitutions produce an activated protein that participates in oncogenesis across multiple tissues [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"].

## Signaling Function

The KRAS product operates downstream to drive crucial cellular processes [26: "stimulate downstream signaling pathways, including cell proliferation and survival"]. Oncogenic mutations lead to persistent signaling that supports tumor initiation and malignant progression [26: "constitutive activation of the KRAS protein, which acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways, including cell proliferation and survival, thereby leading to tumorigenesis"].

The gene symbol is KRAS [1]. The gene product functions as a small GTPase, as the gene encodes a member of the small GTPase superfamily [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. The OMIM title records KRAS PROTOONCOGENE, GTPase; KRAS [4].

## Gene and Sequence Variants

The gene name is KRAS [5]. The literature entity name is Kras [6]. An entry lists NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.458ATG[1] (p.Asp154del) [3]. Another ClinVar record designates NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.36T>C (p.Gly12=) [10]. One sequence variant is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.337C>T (p.Leu113=) [15]. A further ClinVar entry specifies NM_033360.4(KRAS):c.524A>G (p.Glu175Gly) [19]. An additional variant entry is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.417T>A (p.Ile139=) [23].

## Oncogenic Signaling and Biology

A publication is Role of oncogenic KRAS in the prognosis, diagnosis and treatment of colorectal cancer [2]. The publication identifier is 34742312 [8]. Mutated KRAS functions as a molecular switch activating downstream proliferative pathways in colorectal tumors [26: "acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways, including cell proliferation and survival, thereby leading to tumorigenesis"]. A paper title is Oncogenic KRAS Drives Lipofibrogenesis to Promote Angiogenesis and Colon Cancer Progression [14]. That work is indexed under 37768068 [17]. Oncogenic KRAS alters the phenotype of cancer-associated fibroblasts to produce VEGFA and drive vascularization [28: "KRAS* transforms the phenotype of carcinoma-associated fibroblasts (CAF) into lipid-laden CAFs, promoting angiogenesis and tumor progression"].

## Therapeutic Targeting and Degradation

A study title is KRAS mutation: from undruggable to druggable in cancer [9]. Its publication identifier is 34776511 [13]. Direct targeting of the G12C form advanced with the clinical approval of AMG510 [27: "AMG510 was the first drug-targeting KRAS (G12C) to be approved for clinical use this year"]. Another article is Targeting KRAS in pancreatic cancer [18]. It is linked to 38686056 [21]. While cysteine-reactive inhibitors target G12C, other alleles such as G12D require distinct agents like MRTX1133 [29: "most common KRAS mutations in PDAC are G12D (44%), G12V (34%) and G12R (20%) that are not amenable to treatment by KRAS G12C-directed cysteine-reactive KRAS inhibitors"][29: "KRAS G12D-directed MRTX1133 inhibitor has entered clinical trials"]. A paper is titled Targeting cancer with small-molecule pan-KRAS degraders [22]. Its publication identifier is 39298590 [25]. A heterobifunctional degrader was designed to target most major oncogenic variants [30: "designed a heterobifunctional small molecule that potently degrades 13 out of 17 of the most prevalent oncogenic KRAS alleles"].

## Associated Clinical Studies

A trial is Sorafenib in Combination With Irinotecan in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patients With KRAS Mutated Tumors [7]. Another registered study is PREMIUM, Observational Study [12]. Investigators initiated A Trial of mFOLFIRI With MEK162 in Patients With Advanced RAS (HRAS, NRAS, or KRAS) Positive Metastatic Colorectal Cancers [16]. A cohort investigation is Frequency of EGFR and KRAS Mutations and Clinical-prognostic Correlation in Brazilian Lung Cancer Patients [20]. One clinical study is A Phase 1/2, Study Evaluating the Safety, Tolerability, PK, and Efficacy of Sotorasib (AMG 510) in Subjects With Solid Tumors With a Specific KRAS Mutation (CodeBreaK 100) [24].
